class_guess: Bell eats counter: FractalBEC-like 101/00 bouncer plus a 3-cell binary counter with transparent J blocks; the bell shifts the counter one cell
summary: Gap bounces in (101)^a 00 (101)^b, counter counts; at b=0 the low digits pick eat E or bell B0/B1
mechanism: Hub `K(a,b,G) = 0^inf (101)^a 00 (101)^b A> 0 enc(G) 0^inf` (enc 0=000, 1=010, J=100). R1: each bounce moves the 00 gap one block right and adds 1 to the counter G (J skipped).
At b=0 the low digits decide: `0 1^r J^k` = partial eat E (J's become k-1 fresh blocks); `0 1^r 0` / `1...` = bell B0/B1: sweep to the left end, counter shifted one cell (σ).
σ leaves x/z/w marks that the carry cleans within 2^q <= 2^floor(log2 N) increments (19,773/19,773 macro epochs); lockstep from blank holds to 1e9 (all hubs) and 3e10 (b=0 hubs).

rules.name: R1 bounce
rules.cases: a >= 0, b >= 0, G in {0,1}{0,1,J}*; inc = +1 on the digit groups (LSB first), J skipped, a new top digit appended after the last group; a = 0 is the bell sweep to the left end. Orbit: 189,846/189,846 to 1e9

rules.name: R1x bounce on marked words
rules.from: K(a, b+1, G), G with x/z/w groups
rules.cases: T = the counter's own carry transducer, the same for every a, b (x -> z on a carry; z then x-runs -> 0 J... on the next). Orbit: 2,196/2,196 to 1e9

rules.name: E partial eat
rules.cases: r >= 0, k >= 1, G' empty or starting with a digit. Orbit: 229/229 to 1e9

rules.name: B0 bell (low digit 0)
rules.cases: r >= 0, also G = 0 1^r with nothing after; σ = shift every 1-cell of enc one cell left. Orbit: 36/36 to 1e9

template.module: Section FractalBEC, instance tm1 / nonhalt1, cert1 B D [1] [0] [0;1] [1;0;1] [0;0] (mirrored L<->R)
template.note: Same bouncer: w1 = 101, w0 = 00, and the gap step of R1 is the template's RInc. The counter differs: 3-cell digits 000/010 with transparent J = 100 blocks instead of 2-cell digits (LInc not run on ours: the encoding does not match). No overflow Ov and no fractal recursion: the b=0 step is E/B0/B1 by the low digits, with the one-cell shift σ, and epoch lengths are irregular (2, 5, 6, 11, 18, 44, ...) instead of 2^i - 1. Same family as R2 (BECv1 tm108 twin: 'drop a suffix, shift one cell' eat, pending-size invariant).

strategy:
Proof plan: K(a,b,G) with G an Inductive group list; R1 by a carry lemma (ind over digits, J transparent); E/B0/B1 as finite case lemmas with σ as a list shift.
Invariant: G is standard at every b=0 hub. Open: the cleanup lemma on σ-words (x -> z on the first carry, z x^j -> 0 J^(j+1) on the second; time 2^(p+1) <= N).
Start from FractalBEC.v for the bouncer and a BECv1-style digit list for the counter; share the size lemma with R2.
risks: Cleanup lemma unproved: arbitrary x/z/w words halt (K(5,6,1z0101) halts in 19 steps), so the invariant must track where σ puts x/w.
The carry through z/w is a cell-level transducer with context (z followed by x-runs); formalizing it may take many small lemmas.
Same family as R2 and the #10/#30 sibling, which got stuck on a size invariant; that invariant may be hard here too.

checkpoint_questions.text: Hub rows: does each block of rows read as one epoch (the cyan gap walks right through the grey blocks while the white/grey digits between the orange J columns count up), with the low digits eaten at each cyan bar?
Close-up from K(5,2,0JJ1): do you see two bounces, then the partial eat E (the right end jumps left, the two J blocks become one new block), one more bounce, then the bell B1 running to the far left?

Confidence is med: everything to 3e10 fits R1/E/B0/B1, but the cleanup lemma (x/z/w gone before the next b=0) is only observed. Should we fund a proof-prep stage on it, shared with R2's size invariant, or park R3?

status_reason: Med confidence: rules R1/E/B0/B1 cover every hub from blank (lockstep to 1e9, b=0 hubs to 3e10, macro to N=192,042); non-halting still needs the cleanup lemma for x/z/w words. Not a cryptid: the eat choice is a regular function of the low digits.
